newsitem.title: USA: Inland says to begin layoffs soon.
newsitem.headline: Inland says to begin layoffs soon.

text.p: Inland Steel Industries Inc will begin laying off about 450 salaried workers in the next several weeks, starting its planned workforce reduction, Jay Gratz, the company's chief financial officer, said Thursday.
"We will begin (layoffs) shortly," he told reporters in a brief conference call. "(The layoffs) will be across the salaried range."
Gratz declined to be specific about what positions would be affected and when the layoffs would begin, but he indicated they would start in the next several weeks.
Inland Steel Industries currently has 15,700 employees. Its steelmaking unit, Inland Steel Co, by far its largest unit, has 10,700 employees.
Gratz said the layoffs are necessary to help the company cut costs and remain competitive in the steel industry.
The company on Thursday posted a fourth quarter loss of $0.03 per share, which included a $0.35 per share provision to account for the workforce reduction.
In the fourth quarter of '95 the company posted earnings of $0.47 per share.
Inland shares were up 1/8 to 19-3/8 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Gratz said steel prices in '96 were "down substantially" from '95 levels, causing the company to post an operating profit in the fourth quarter of $22.5 million. Operating profit in the fourth quarter of '95 was $57.9 million.
He declined to comment on contract prices in '96, citing ongoing supply negotiations with automakers, who are large contract customers.
Contract customers account for about 60 percent of the company's business.
